questions.a: Two named. (1) 'Start the device' is definable per device — standing, via a lifecycle declaration on the device class defaulting to 'no separate process' (a calibre-shaped device reports that `start` is a no-op). (2) The STATUS and SETTINGS panes are the same data as the web panes — RULED 2026-09-06 on 15d6a0ef9c11, so not an assumption. Neither is load-bearing beyond the build.

One point was asserted wrapped and was not: what a non-hot answer on a stopped device is made of. Now wrapped: the shim's last-known state (introspect()['state'] as held), marked `cached: true` with its timestamp, and 'never run' if there is none. And `restart` from the groundloop verbs ticket has no ruled root — it becomes stop+start, recorded as a supersession in vocabulary.

Consulted the lab. 15d6a0ef9c11 is the vocabulary at PROVEME; this is its build, cast as a child rather than widening a ticket past its cursor. 5ef45e513849 cairn-groundloop-stop-start-restart-status (PROVED) is a device-local precursor: superseded in vocabulary (restart), re-homed in function; its proof stays green because stop+start is what restart did. Recursive-CLI-resolution (each segment resolves its children; no master index) is served — bin/cairn still knows no verbs. No Law collides.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) the verb table and each verb's source — show/get: declared_views() in cairn/tools/base/device.py (exists); list: the keys of declared_views() plus declared_panes(); settings: introspect()['settings'] or the literal 'No settings'; start/stop: a new `lifecycle` declaration on BaseDevice (default: none); (b) `hot` handling — strip it from the verb line, set a flag, and if the device is not running call start before the view; (c) where — one `resolve(verbs)` on BaseShim, and `cairn/devices/*/shim.py` must not override it; (d) the human format for `show` — the existing pane renderer the web server uses, not a new one; (e) don't — no new verbs, no per-device parsing, no `restart`. All written into the ticket's how.
